subject: Admin activity ledger export — Parquet vs JSONL, manifest & attestations
messages:

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Admin activity ledger export - file formats and manifest expectations

Hi Karthik,

We're preparing for a SIG + SOC2 audit and need clarification on the admin-activity evidence Redwood can deliver for NovaMed. Two quick questions to start: 1) Can you provide the admin-ledger exports as Parquet (columnar) or do you only provide gzipped JSONL/NDJSON? 2) What do your manifests include — do you provide a signed manifest with per-file SHA256 checksums, schema/field definitions, partitioning info, and a chain-of-custody attestation?

A few constraints from our auditors: exports must include event-level timestamps (UTC), actor identity (internal user id + email), event_type (login, token_create, role_change, api_key_rotate, deployment_change, model_pin), and object identifiers. We also need to know retention windows you support for raw operator logs vs. derived audit ledger.

Can you point us to a sample manifest and confirm whether Redwood supports Parquet with an Avro/Parquet schema, or whether we should expect JSONL only? If Parquet is available, auditors want to validate partitioning (date/hour) and checksum strategy.

Thanks — if easier, we can do a 20-minute call with your infra team.

Dana Sparks
Head of Compliance, NovaMed Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Admin activity ledger export - file formats and manifest expectations

Dana —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers first: we support both gzipped line-delimited JSON (JSONL/NDJSON) and Parquet exports; both are first-class for admin-activity exports. We also provide manifest files that include per-file SHA256 checksums, file sizes, logical partitions (yyyy/mm/dd/hour), a top-level schema reference (Avro/Parquet or JSON Schema), and a signed attest token (HMAC-SHA256) for chain-of-custody verification.

What we typically deliver for SOC 2 / SIG evidence:
- Scope: admin-auth events (login, MFA changes), API key lifecycle (create/rotate/revoke), RBAC changes (role grants/revokes), operator console actions (model pin/unpin, rollout changes, capacity scale, config changes), audit policy changes, and provisioning actions.
- Formats: JSONL.gz (utf-8) for event-level exports, or Parquet files with embedded Avro schema for columnar workloads. Parquet helps downstream auditors run column-level queries faster.
- Partitioning: date/hour partitions by default; hourly slices to keep file sizes manageable.
- Manifest: top-level manifest.jsonl (newline-delimited) listing blobs with fields: file_path, sha256, size_bytes, record_count, partition_key, schema_id, exported_at, signed_by (service principal). We attach an HMAC-SHA256 signature (key rotation supported) and can optionally provide a signed envelope from our KMS.
- Retention: operator events retained 365 days by default for hosted customers; we can adjust (shorten or extend) by contract for Dedicated/Private. For audit evidence packages we provide on-demand full-scope bundles (attested) and incremental snapshots for delta deliveries.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Kim (cc) from infra/security can confirm encryption/KMS details and the signed-attestation flow; 2) Marissa (cc) can coordinate the evidence delivery (S3 presigned, transfer window, and manifest proof). If you want, we can spin up a sample export into your S3 staging bucket for auditors to inspect.

Attaching: sample_admin_schema.avsc (Avro) and an export_manifest_example.jsonl stub so your team can review field names.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Admin activity ledger export - file formats and manifest expectations

Hi Dana / Karthik —

Following up with the infra/security specifics you asked for. Key points:

1) Export job mechanics
- We can create an export job that writes directly to your S3 staging path (s3://novamed-audit-staging/DEAL-4832/) using roles you provide, or push to our bucket and issue presigned URLs for bulk transfer.
- Files are written as either: parquet (snappy) + .parquet, or gzip-compressed jsonl (.jsonl.gz).

2) Schema & partitioning
- Parquet exports use an Avro schema (attached sample_avro.avsc) and preserve event-level timestamp as ts_utc (ISO8601) and actor_id / actor_email as separate fields.
- We partition by yyyy/mm/dd/hour and include a zero-padded hour folder (00..23). Hourly shards keep each file < 4GB typical.

3) Manifest & checksums
- Manifest is newline-delimited JSON (manifest.jsonl) with entries: {"file_path","sha256","size_bytes","record_count","partition_key","schema_id","exported_at"}. Example attached in export_manifest_example.jsonl.
- We provide SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest token. For higher assurance we can sign the manifest with our KMS-backed key and provide the public key/certificate chain.

4) Attestation & chain-of-custody
- For SOC 2 evidence we provide an attestation envelope: signed manifest + job-run metadata (initiated_by, job_id, start/end timestamps) and a transfer_log showing presigned URL issuance and retrieval timestamps.

5) Retention & redaction
- Live operator events: default 365 days.
- Evidence bundles for audits: we create a timeboxed snapshot and can optionally apply PII redaction rules or provide sampled and fully redacted copies per auditor request.

If you'd like, I can schedule the export job for tomorrow and share a presigned staging location for your auditors. Confirm whether you want Parquet (recommended) or JSONL for initial review.

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
